input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets our preferred position in full. 21.1 sets a single mutual cap at the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim event and (b) USD 1,000,000, expressly stated to be mutual — neither party is uncapped and the basis is "paid or payable" rather than the narrower "paid". The "Fees" definition (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees (not an illusory set-up fee), and §2.1 commits USD 2,000,000 of annual spend, so the fee-based limb is meaningful. 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually and helpfully confirms data restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs are direct damages. 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP outside the cap, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages". No competing cap or one-sided liability language appears elsewhere (§18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). Separate note for the indemnity rule: Section 20 (indemnification, cross-referenced in §9.3 and §21.3) is absent from the document, so the indemnity carve-out currently has nothing to attach to; that gap is outside the scope of this cap rule and no redline to Section 21 is warranted.
